report.clinical_summary: 55-year-old male with CLL diagnosed several years ago, early stage, stable without treatment. Presents with new left-sided neck lymphadenopathy (pea-sized, firm, attached to skin, non-movable) and gradually increasing fatigue over the past few months. Takes a multivitamin but no CLL-specific medication. No other chronic conditions, no recent infections, no family history of lymph node issues. Trusts healthcare providers and is agreeable to follow-up testing.

evidence.quote: I've just been feeling a bit more drained lately. It's not like I'm completely exhausted or anything, but I definitely notice that I need a little extra rest after work. It doesn't really interfere with my activities during the day, but I find myself dozing off on the couch when I get home.

consequences.reasoning: He keeps his roles but has changed how he does them - needs extra rest, dozes off on couch. This fits the 4 scale (keeps their roles but has changed how they do them: pacing, hours, help with the heavy parts).

evidence.quote: I haven't needed any medication yet, just regular follow-up appointments every three months and occasional blood work to keep an eye on my counts.

timeline.reasoning: Plans are built around ongoing monitoring rather than treatment. He accepts the current management approach (watchful waiting) as appropriate for early-stage CLL. This fits the 8 scale (plans on the assumption it stays. Arrangements are built around it continuing).

evidence.quote: I trust that we'll figure out what's going on. And if it is related to my CLL, then I know you'll take care of me and help manage the condition.

personal_control.reasoning: He trusts healthcare providers to manage the condition. No mention of self-management strategies or personal agency in influencing disease course. This fits the 2 scale (takes no action of their own; the outcome belongs to luck, fate or the doctors).
